content: {"rules": ["Forecast models consistently overestimate prices in early cycles, indicating a lag in adjusting to true market sentiment.", "Sentiment spikes often precede price corrections, suggesting a feedback loop between sentiment and price overshoot.", "Model forecasts show mean-reversion bias, especially when sentiment turns negative, leading to premature price declines.", "High sentiment positivity correlates with forecast overestimation, implying sentiment amplifies model bias.", "Price corrections are more pronounced when sentiment is mixed or negative, indicating sentiment-driven volatility.", "Forecast accuracy improves when sentiment aligns with recent price trends, suggesting sentiment validates model assumptions.", "Models fail to capture sharp reversals when sentiment shifts abruptly, indicating sensitivity to sentiment timing.", "Forecast lags are most severe during sentiment volatility, suggesting sentiment-driven momentum is not fully reflected in early predictions."]}
